author: @superm1

evidence.api_compatibility: No API changes. The three touched files are a CI workflow (`.github/workflows/docs_and_style.yml`), a vendor README (`src/app/src/renderer/vendor/README.md`), and a new sidecar hash file (`src/app/src/renderer/vendor/model-viewer.min.js.sha256`). Zero lines deleted from production code. The vendored bundle is unchanged.
evidence.documentation: The vendor README was rewritten comprehensively: it documents the hash chain (npm tarball integrity → extracted-file SHA-256), the integrity values, and the full secure update process with error handling and cleanup. The CI job includes an explanatory comment describing it as a drift guard. The update script is copy-paste ready with `set -euo pipefail`, `mktemp`, and a `trap` for cleanup. Version number updated from 4.3.0 to 4.3.1. No documentation gaps.
evidence.manual_release_testing: No user-facing behavioral change. The bundle version (4.3.1) matches what was already in the file — the diff contains no changes to `model-viewer.min.js` itself. The CI drift guard and documented update process protect against future drift but do not alter the shipped artifact. This commit is purely documentation, a new CI job, and a new sidecar hash file.
evidence.post_approval_commits: None. @fl0rianr approved commit 34e848a5 at 2026-09-09T19:12:11Z. The merge completed at 2026-09-10T00:14:06Z with no new commits. The PR was in the merge group for a few hours before landing. No post-approval churn whatsoever.
evidence.review: PR #2709 received six substantive reviews from @fl0rianr over six weeks (Jul 15 – Sep 9). @fl0rianr holds security and CI as a subject area per contribute.md, and the review applied the project philosophy (designing for agility through automated integrity checks, treating user-facing bugs like the shadow regression as critical). The review chain: CHANGES_REQUESTED on the initial diff for accidentally reverting google/model-viewer#5168 (shadow mapping fix for models > 1×1); COMMENTED to require pinning the official 4.3.1 release instead; COMMENTED to fix the update script's integrity comparison (EXPECTED used `sha512-<base64>` but ACTUAL used `sha512:<hex>` — the script would have rejected every correct tarball); COMMENTED to add fail-closed behavior (`set -euo pipefail`, fresh `mktemp -d` extraction dir); and finally APPROVED on the last commit. Review quality is excellent. No post-approval commits exist. No commits were added after @fl0rianr's approval on 2026-09-09T19:12:11Z.
evidence.security: This is a legitimate security hardening change. @superm1 replaced the vendor README's download-and-replace pattern with a secure update process that verifies npm's published `dist.integrity` (SHA-512) before extracting the tarball — exactly the trust chain the README documents. @fl0rianr correctly caught that the initial script compared integrity hashes using mismatched formats (base64 vs hex) which would have silently accepted tampered tarballs. The CI drift guard (SHA-256 `sha256sum -c`) is honestly described as a drift guard, not a true SRI replacement, which is technically accurate: the asset and checksum can be co-modified in the same commit. The npm dist.integrity is the real upstream anchor. Supply-chain risk is reduced.
evidence.tests: The vendored-asset-integrity job was added to `.github/workflows/docs_and_style.yml` and runs `sha256sum -c model-viewer.min.js.sha256` on every CI run. All checks passed on the final commit (including the new vendored-asset-integrity job). CodeQL, server build, unit tests, CLI tests, and API tests all passed. The PR also resolves a rendering regression (shadow mapping fix from upstream #5168) by pinning 4.3.1, so existing Tauri app tests exercising the 3D panel validate that behavior.

shout_outs.reason: Caught a critical rendering regression (upstream shadow mapping fix being accidentally reverted), identified a broken integrity comparison in the update script that would have accepted tampered tarballs, and drove the PR to fail-closed through six substantive reviews over six weeks.
